description:
You are an economist verifying whether a linear regression of food expenditure on income is correctly specified.

Using the food expenditure dataset (food.gdt) already loaded in Gretl, perform the following analysis and save ALL results to a single output file:

1. Estimate the linear OLS model: food_exp on a constant and income
2. Perform Ramsey's RESET test on this linear model (using the default specification with squared and cubed fitted values)
3. Generate log transformations of both variables (l_food_exp = ln(food_exp) and l_income = ln(income))
4. Estimate the log-linear OLS model: l_food_exp on a constant and l_income
5. Save ALL output (both model estimation results AND the RESET test results) to the file:
   /home/ga/Documents/gretl_output/reset_comparison.txt

The output file must contain:
- The linear model coefficients, standard errors, and R-squared
- The RESET test statistic and p-value
- The log-linear model coefficients, standard errors, and R-squared

You may use the Gretl console, the script editor, or the GUI menus. One convenient approach is to use the Gretl console (Tools > Gretl console) or script editor to redirect output. For example, in a gretl script you can use commands like:
  open /home/ga/Documents/gretl_data/food.gdt
  ols food_exp const income
  reset
  logs food_exp income
  ols l_food_exp const l_income
and redirect the output appropriately.

The key requirement is that all results end up in /home/ga/Documents/gretl_output/reset_comparison.txt
